name: gwyllion

attributes.attribute: an old hag with a wooden milk-pail
wore ash-gray rags and a flat hat
vanished at the sight of iron or a knife

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The gwyllion is a figure from Welsh folklore. This old spirit haunted lonely roads in Wales. She came as an old hag with a wooden milk-pail in hand. Her apron hung over one shoulder, and she wore ash-colored rags and a flat, four-cornered hat. No record says she attacked the people she met on the road. Her look alone could frighten a traveler. Like other fairy folk, she feared metal. The sight of iron, a knife, or any cutlery made her vanish at once.

okr.objective: Describe the gwyllion, a Welsh ghost that haunted lonely roads.
key_results: The source places the gwyllion on lonely roads in Wales.
